prior_stories.headline: Lowell knocks out power across Kauai
prior_stories.body:
Hurricane Lowell passed near Hawaii’s western islands, leaving about 90% of Kauai utility customers without power.

Officials reported downed trees, damaged roads and widespread infrastructure damage as the island experienced heavy rain, damaging winds and coastal flooding.

prior_stories.headline: U.S. destroys five Iranian oil tankers
prior_stories.body:
U.S. forces destroyed five Iranian crude-oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman. U.S. Central Command said the strikes followed two attempted ballistic-missile attacks on an American Navy warship.

Officials said the tankers’ crews were warned to abandon the vessels before they were struck.

prior_stories.headline: Houthi strikes wound 73 in Saudi Arabia
prior_stories.body:
Houthi attacks across Saudi Arabia wounded 73 people and started fires at oil facilities and utilities.

The strikes included an attack near Jazan, which is home to one of the country’s largest refineries.

prior_stories.headline: Canada tariffs take effect as U.S. retaliates
prior_stories.body:
Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion in U.S. imports.

The United States announced that it would ban most Canadian alcoholic beverages, some dairy products and motorcycles beginning September 29. It also moved to exclude Canadian goods from large federal contracts.

prior_stories.headline: British air traffic failure cancels 1,000 flights
prior_stories.body:
A failure in Britain’s flight-processing system disrupted 15 airports and caused more than 1,000 cancellations.

National Air Traffic Services restored the system that evening, but delays continued as airlines worked through the backlog.

prior_stories.headline: Brazilian justice removes police, intelligence chiefs
prior_stories.body:
Brazilian Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça ordered the removal of the country’s federal police and intelligence chiefs amid an escalating conflict within the court.

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government appealed the order. The dispute comes ahead of Brazil’s national elections in October.

candidates.title: IAEA refers Iran to U.N. Security Council
candidates.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency’s governing board reported Iran to the U.N. Security Council for failing to cooperate with an investigation into uranium traces at undeclared sites. It was the agency’s first such referral of Iran in 20 years; 23 of the board’s 35 countries supported the resolution.

candidates.title: Iran fires missiles at U.S.-used base in Jordan
candidates.summary: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said it launched ballistic missiles at the Al-Azraq base in Jordan in retaliation for U.S. attacks on Iranian oil tankers. Jordan said its air defenses intercepted 18 of 20 missiles and that the other two landed in unpopulated areas without causing casualties.

candidates.title: Oil rises above $100 a barrel
candidates.summary: Global benchmark oil prices climbed above $100 a barrel as fighting involving the United States and Iran threatened energy production and shipping. U.S. stocks fell and gasoline prices continued to rise.

candidates.title: Trump administration proposes major census changes
candidates.summary: The Commerce Department proposed counting only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents for congressional apportionment in the 2030 census. The proposal would exclude undocumented immigrants and many people lawfully present on temporary visas, potentially changing the allocation of House seats and federal funding.

candidates.title: Temporary protected status expires for Salvadorans
candidates.summary: The U.S. Temporary Protected Status designation covering roughly 200,000 Salvadoran immigrants expired without an announced extension. The program had protected eligible Salvadorans from deportation and authorized them to work in the United States.

candidates.title: Missouri congressional map dispute returns to Supreme Court
candidates.summary: A group opposing Missouri’s new Republican-drawn congressional map asked the U.S. Supreme Court to block a federal judge’s order requiring its use in November. The order conflicted with a Missouri Supreme Court ruling that the map never took effect and must be submitted to voters in a referendum.

candidates.title: Trump promises conditional $5,000 payments to adults
candidates.summary: President Donald Trump told the Republican midterm convention that every adult American would receive $5,000 if Republicans retained control of both chambers of Congress in November. He did not provide details about funding or implementation.

candidates.title: Apple introduces its first foldable iPhone
candidates.summary: Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, alongside updated conventional iPhones, watches and AirPods. The announcement marked Apple’s entry into the foldable-phone market under new chief executive John Ternus.

candidates.title: Astronomers identify new class of X-ray objects
candidates.summary: Scientists using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory reported finding 84 objects across six galaxies that emit unusually low-energy X-rays and intense ultraviolet radiation. The researchers classified them as hypersoft X-ray sources, a previously unknown class that may involve compact stars drawing material from companions.

candidates.title: NASA adds Terran R to launch-services contract
candidates.summary: NASA added Relativity Space’s reusable Terran R rocket to its launch-services contract, making the vehicle eligible to compete for future NASA and other federal missions. The contract’s ordering period runs through June 2030.

candidates.title: DOJ opens investigation into Los Angeles jail conditions
candidates.summary: The Justice Department opened a civil-rights investigation into whether conditions at Los Angeles County’s Men’s Central Jail violate constitutional and federal standards. The inquiry will focus on whether the facility provides safe, humane and habitable conditions rather than on the conduct of individual deputies.

candidates.title: Tate brothers denied release during extradition case
candidates.summary: A federal magistrate judge in Miami ordered social-media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate to remain in custody while they contest extradition to the United Kingdom, where they face allegations including rape and sex trafficking. The brothers deny wrongdoing.

sources.name: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida

candidates.title: Russian and Ukrainian strikes cause casualties
candidates.summary: Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine killed at least two people and wounded seven, while a later drone strike in Sumy killed three more. Ukrainian drones struck the Russian port of Novorossiysk, where regional officials reported four deaths and 29 injuries; Ukraine said the targets included a naval base and oil-loading terminal.

candidates.title: U.K. flight cancellations surpass 2,000
candidates.summary: The number of flights canceled following a failure in Britain’s air-traffic flight-processing system rose above 2,000. Airlines continued rebooking passengers and repositioning aircraft after the system was restored.

candidates.title: California man receives 30-year sentence for Medi-Cal fraud
candidates.summary: A federal judge sentenced Paul Richard Randall to 30 years in prison for orchestrating a scheme that submitted nearly $270 million in fraudulent prescription-drug claims to California’s Medicaid program. He was also ordered to pay about $178.7 million in restitution.

stories.headline: Iran fires 20 missiles at base in Jordan
stories.body:
Iran launched ballistic missiles at Jordan’s Al-Azraq base, which is used by the U.S. military. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said the attack was retaliation for U.S. strikes on Iranian oil tankers.

Jordan said its air defenses intercepted 18 of the 20 missiles. The other two landed in unpopulated areas, and no casualties were reported.

stories.headline: Oil tops $100 amid U.S.-Iran fighting
stories.body:
Global benchmark oil prices climbed above $100 a barrel as fighting involving the United States and Iran threatened energy production and shipping.

U.S. gasoline prices continued to rise, while stocks fell.

stories.headline: Protections expire for 200,000 Salvadorans
stories.body:
Temporary Protected Status expired for roughly 200,000 Salvadoran immigrants in the United States, with no extension announced.

The program had protected eligible Salvadorans from deportation and authorized them to work in the country. Its expiration ends those protections for recipients without another legal status.

exclusions.reason: Source says protections remain pending a decision.
Reported at 02:54 September 9 in Jordan, before September 9 began in New York.
